sender.en: Your boss, a director or a supplier

name.en: Fake boss or supplier email asking for an urgent payment

how.en: Scammers pretend to be a company’s chief executive or director, or a supplier, and email staff to pay an invoice or send money to a new account. The request is urgent and often confidential. Maltese companies lost millions this way in 2025; some found out only months later.

text.en: An email that seems to come from the boss or a supplier arrives.
It asks for an urgent payment or gives new bank details.
It asks you to keep it quiet or not to call.
The money goes to the scammers’ account.

Hi Mark, are you at your desk? I need a payment processed before noon for a deal we’re closing, €48,500 to the account in the attached invoice. Keep this between us until it’s announced. I’m in meetings so email only. Thanks, David

en: email from the CEO asking for a payment
boss asked me to keep the payment quiet
An urgent or secret payment request by email.
New bank details for a supplier sent by email.
The sender can’t be reached by phone.
Confirm by phone on a number you already know, never the one in the email.
If money was sent, call your bank straight away to try to stop it.

sources.title: Police investigated €13 million worth of scams in first 6 months this year
